title: Single-station CNN analysis adds 273 visually confirmed earthquakes to the L’Aquila near-fault catalog
summary: A two-stage 1D CNN pipeline applied to continuous three-component seismic waveforms from one L’Aquila station identified 273 previously uncataloged local earthquake events during a one-month 2009 foreshock period. The study reports that 84% were assigned magnitude below 1 and that all 273 new detections were visually confirmed; the expanded catalog contained roughly three times as many new detections as the pre-existing catalog had events for that period.
ai_technology: Two-stage one-dimensional convolutional neural network (CNN) pipeline

evidence.tested: A two-stage 1D CNN pipeline applied to continuous three-component seismic waveforms from one L’Aquila station identified 273 previously uncataloged local earthquake events during a one-month 2009 foreshock period.
evidence.unknown: The analysis covers one month in February 2009 from one station. The authors report 273 new local detections and six nonlocal events among 369 windows classified as local; all 273 new detections were visually confirmed. The pipeline does not provide exact event locations, and transfer to other regions was not established. Magnitudes are coarse classes, not precise estimates.
evidence.ai_role: The detector CNN scanned continuous raw three-component waveform windows for earthquake signals; a second CNN classified distance and magnitude, enabling the researchers to find and characterize uncataloged events from a single station. The CNN pipeline generated the new event detections; authors then visually checked them.
